name.en-US: Of Interior Peace, or The Path to Paradise
name.it: Della pace interiore, o Sentiero del Paradiso (trad. inglese 1875)
name.pt-BR: Da paz interior, ou O caminho do Paraíso

description.en-US: The short treatise of Scupoli on interior peace, called the Path to Paradise: how to govern the heart, keep a peaceful spirit under temptation, and walk the road of the cross with confidence in God. English translation of 1875; the Italian is not yet imported.
description.it: Il breve trattato di Scupoli sulla pace interiore, detto Sentiero del Paradiso. Traduzione inglese del 1875; l’originale italiano non è ancora importato.
description.pt-BR: O breve tratado de Scupoli sobre a paz interior, chamado Caminho do Paraíso. Tradução inglesa de 1875.

en-US.translator: Anonymous (Library of Spiritual Works for English Catholics, London: Rivingtons)

sources.edition: The Spiritual Combat, a new translation, Library of Spiritual Works for English Catholics, London/Oxford/Cambridge: Rivingtons, 1875. English Wikisource transcription (proofread from scan index Spiritualcombat.djvu).
sources.description: The chapters of Of Interior Peace, or the Path to Paradise. The series was Anglo-Catholic, but the Catholic content is kept. The Italian original of this piece (Venice 1770 and other collected editions) exists only as long-s OCR and is not imported.
sources.tierEvidence: Published 1875 by an anonymous translator: public domain in the US (before 1931).

title.en-US: Chapter I. What is the Nature of our Heart, and how it ought to be Governed
Chapter II. Of the Care we should have to preserve a Peaceful Spirit
Chapter III. How this Building of Inward Peace must be gradually constructed
Chapter IV. How the Soul must refuse all Consolations, for this is true Humility and Poverty of Spirit, by which Interior Peace is acquired
Chapter V. How the Soul should keep herself in a state of inward Solitude, that God may work within her
Chapter VI. Of the Prudence which we ought to exercise in the Love of our Neighbour, so as not to disturb this Peace
Chapter VII. How the Soul, despoiled of its own Will, must present itself before God
Chapter VIII. Of the Faith we should have in the Most Holy Sacrament of the Altar; and how we should Offer ourselves unto the Lord
Chapter IX. That we ought not to seek Pleasures, nor the things which gratify our Tastes; but God Alone
Chapter X. That the Servant of God must not be Discouraged, though he feel within himself some Repugnance and Disquiet as to this Peace
Chapter XI. Of the Diligence which the Devil employs to disturb this Peace, and how we ought to guard ourselves against his Devices
Chapter XII. That the Soul ought not to Disquiet itself on account of inward Trials
Chapter XIII. That Temptations are sent us by God for our good
Chapter XIV. Of the Remedy which we ought to use, so as not to be disquieted under Faults and Infirmities
Chapter XV. How the Soul, without loss of Time, should recover Calmness, and make Progress
